roots.context: We have learned that every magnet has a north and a south pole, and that a pushed-away magnet turns round and attracts. Now we ask what that tells us about ourselves and the world.

deep_truth.truth: When two north poles faced each other on the water, the magnets pushed apart. Then one turned round, and they snapped together, north to south. Magnets that are free to turn always end up attracting. Repelling lasts only while something holds them facing the wrong way.
deep_truth.habit: We think of attract and repel as two equal and opposite things a magnet does. But they are one force, and which one you get depends only on which way the magnets face. Left free, magnets turn to attract.
deep_truth.evidence: In the Magnet Boats test, boats that started north facing north pushed apart, turned and stuck together. Ring magnets float on a pencil only while the pencil stops them turning. Samuel Earnshaw proved in 1842 that ordinary magnets on their own cannot hold a magnet floating still.

three.who_am_i: You felt the push between two magnets with your own hands. You can sense a force you cannot see.
three.what_is_life: Some bacteria live in mud and need to find the parts low in oxygen. They carry a chain of tiny magnet crystals, joined north to south. The chain turns them along the Earth's magnetic field, which slopes down into the ground, so swimming along it takes them deeper.
three.what_is_this_world: The Earth is a giant magnet with two poles. Every compass needle on Earth turns to line up with them.

roots.thread: A magnet's north and south poles are never apart. Cut a magnet, and each piece has both again. Inside, countless tiny magnets point the same way and add up to one force. That one force shows up in many ways: a push, a pull, a turn, a needle pointing north. Underneath the many things magnets do is one force, and it settles into attraction when nothing holds it back.

teachings.teaching: Long and short shape each other. High and low lean on each other. Front and back follow each other.
teachings.link: A north pole never exists without a south pole. Cut a magnet, and both appear again at the cut. Each pole needs the other.

teachings.source: Heraclitus, fragment B51 (Diels-Kranz numbering), about 500 BCE
teachings.teaching: People do not see how something pulling apart also holds together, like the bow and the lyre, held in shape by strings pulling against them.
teachings.link: Two repelling magnets are a balance of push and twist that holds only while something keeps them straight. Let go, and the balance turns into attraction.

science.text: Every magnet ever tested has both a north and a south pole.
Ordinary magnets on their own cannot hold another magnet floating still. Samuel Earnshaw proved this in 1842.
Whether a single north or south pole, a monopole, can exist is not known.

other_view.view: A free magnet turns to attract because that is the arrangement with the least stored energy, the same reason a ball rolls downhill. It is a useful rule, not a lesson about the world, and reading meaning into it says more about us than about magnets.

practice.title: Feel the turn
practice.say: Hold one magnet in each hand, north facing north. Bring them close until you feel the push. Hold them there and breathe in slowly three times. Notice how your fingers must work to keep them straight. Now loosen your grip a little. Feel one magnet start to twist. Let it turn, and let the two come together. Breathe out.
practice.kid: Hold two magnets, north facing north. Feel the push. Breathe in three times. Loosen your fingers a little. Feel the twist. Let them turn and join. Breathe out.

playtest: Every activity was walked through as if at home, with the materials listed. Magnet Boats needs two bar magnets with poles at their ends: bendy fridge magnets will not work, because their poles are in stripes. Lids must be plastic and the tub plastic, with the fan off and the tub a metre from the fridge and steel almirahs. A full tub stops lids catching on the side.
